Temanggung Coffee Guide: Export Grades, Specs & Pricing

By IBRAHIM • Friday, June 5, 2026

Temanggung Coffee: Complete Export Guide — Grades, Specifications & Pricing (2025)

Among Indonesia's many celebrated coffee origins — Gayo in Aceh, Mandheling in Sumatra, Bajawa in Flores, Toraja in Sulawesi — Temanggung remains one of the country's most distinctive and commercially undervalued producing regions. Nestled between two active volcanoes in the highlands of Central Java, Temanggung produces both Arabica and Robusta coffees with a flavor identity that is entirely its own: full-bodied, earthy, complex, and marked by an unmistakable tobacco-spice character that no other origin in the world can authentically replicate.

For international buyers — whether specialty importers, commercial roasters, private label distributors, or green bean traders — Temanggung represents a rare combination of genuine origin differentiation, competitive pricing, and a growing base of professional exporter-roasters capable of supplying export-ready roasted product directly to destination markets.

This guide covers everything you need to make informed sourcing decisions: the region's geography and terroir, variety profiles, processing methods, roast specifications, export grade classifications, packaging formats, minimum order quantities, FOB pricing, certifications, and a step-by-step procurement process.

See also: Learn how to choose the right fuel for your robusta coffee bean.

1. Geography and Terroir: Why Temanggung Produces Exceptional Coffee

Temanggung Regency is located in Central Java Province, Indonesia, positioned on the fertile volcanic slopes between Mount Sumbing (3,371 masl) and Mount Sindoro (3,136 masl) — two of Java's most active volcanic peaks. Coffee farms in the region are cultivated at elevations ranging from 800 to 1,600 meters above sea level (masl), with the highest-quality specialty lots typically coming from farms above 1,200 masl.

Key Terroir Factors

FactorDetail
LocationTemanggung Regency, Central Java Province, Indonesia
Coordinates~7°18'S, 110°10'E
Elevation800–1,600 masl (specialty lots: 1,200–1,600 masl)
Soil TypeAndosol (volcanic ash soil) — mineral-rich, excellent drainage
Average Rainfall2,000–3,000 mm/year
Temperature15–24°C average
Total Plantation Area~12,000 hectares
Annual Production~6,000–8,000 metric tonnes (Arabica + Robusta)

The volcanic andosol soils of Mount Sumbing and Sindoro are exceptionally rich in potassium, phosphorus, calcium, and magnesium — nutrients that directly support the development of complex organic compounds in coffee cherries. The cool highland temperatures slow cherry maturation significantly, allowing sugars and flavor precursors to accumulate over a longer development period. This is the agronomic foundation of Temanggung coffee's characteristic depth and complexity.

The Tobacco-Coffee Intercropping Signature

Temanggung is simultaneously one of Indonesia's most important tobacco-producing regencies, and many smallholder farms grow coffee and tobacco side by side on the same volcanic slopes. This intercropping — combined with the cultivation of cloves, cocoa, and other aromatic crops in adjacent fields — is widely credited with contributing to Temanggung coffee's signature tobacco, earthy spice, and herbal complexity. It is a terroir characteristic that is genuinely unique to this region and impossible to replicate elsewhere.

For international buyers building differentiated product portfolios, this origin story is commercially compelling: Temanggung coffee has a provenance narrative that is both authentic and memorable.

2. Coffee Varieties: Robusta and Arabica

Temanggung is one of the few producing regions in Indonesia — and in the world — where both high-quality Robusta and specialty-grade Arabica are cultivated within the same geographical area. Each variety serves different market segments and carries distinct commercial applications.

Temanggung Robusta

Robusta is the dominant variety in Temanggung and the product for which the region has historically been best known among Indonesian coffee traders and European espresso blenders. Cultivated primarily at lower to mid elevations (800–1,200 masl) — significantly higher than most Robusta farms globally — Temanggung Robusta delivers a cup profile that challenges the commodity-grade assumptions most buyers associate with this species.

Flavor Profile:

- Body: Very full, dense, syrupy

- Acidity: Low

- Flavor notes: Dark chocolate, strong cocoa, brown sugar, earthy spice, tobacco, woody smokiness, hints of black pepper

- Aroma: Bold, smoky, deeply aromatic

- Finish: Long, thick, lingering bittersweet

Select Temanggung Robusta lots have been evaluated under the SCA Fine Robusta standard, with cupping scores reaching 80+ from certified Q-Robusta Graders — placing them firmly in the fine/premium tier above commodity-grade product.

Commercial applications: Premium espresso blends (crema-building backbone), traditional café espresso, energy beverage and instant coffee production, Vietnamese-style coffee, single-origin espresso for fine Robusta specialty markets.

Temanggung Arabica

Arabica cultivation in Temanggung is more limited but growing rapidly, concentrated in the higher-elevation sub-districts of Tretep, Wonoboyo, Candiroto, Kledung, and Bansari — typically above 1,200 masl. Common cultivars include Typica, Bourbon, Kartika, Sigarar Utang, and Andungsari, with some farms maintaining older heirloom varieties.

Flavor Profile:

- Body: Medium to full, silky mouthfeel

- Acidity: Low to medium — clean, balanced, approachable

- Flavor notes: Dark chocolate, hazelnut, stone fruit (peach, apricot), orange zest, herbal florality, light tobacco undertones, dried fruits (raisin, tamarind)

- Aroma: Floral, earthy, herbal sweetness

- Finish: Long, clean, pleasant bittersweet cocoa aftertaste

Cup score range: Specialty lots consistently achieve 83–87 SCA points from certified Q Graders; top micro-lots and competition-grade offerings occasionally reach 88+.

Commercial applications: Single-origin espresso, premium filter/pour-over, specialty subscription coffee, private label specialty retail, competition-grade and micro-lot programs.

Comparison with other Indonesian origins: Temanggung Arabica tends to be cleaner, less musty, and more fruit-forward than Sumatran Mandheling — appealing particularly to markets in Scandinavia, Australia, Japan, and the US that favor clarity and complexity over heavy earthiness.

3. Processing Methods and Their Impact on Flavor

Post-harvest processing is one of the most critical determinants of cup quality and flavor profile. Temanggung producers employ multiple processing methods, each producing distinct flavor outcomes. International buyers should specify their preferred processing method clearly when placing orders.

Wet-Hulled / Giling Basah (Most Traditional)

The dominant processing method across Indonesia and the most widely used in Temanggung. Parchment is removed while the bean still has high moisture content (30–40%), and the beans are then dried further. This produces the characteristic Indonesian flavor profile: heavy body, earthy depth, syrupy texture, and low acidity.

Best for: Buyers targeting traditional espresso blends, dark roast markets, Middle Eastern and European institutional buyers, or consumers who specifically seek bold, earthy Javanese-style coffee.

Fully Washed / Wet Process

Increasingly offered by specialty-oriented cooperatives and progressive producers in Temanggung. Complete mucilage removal before drying produces a cleaner, brighter cup with greater clarity, more pronounced acidity, and better-defined fruit notes.

Best for: Specialty roasters, third-wave cafés, pour-over and filter coffee markets, and buyers targeting Japan, Scandinavia, Australia, and the US specialty segment.

Honey Process

A growing trend in Temanggung's specialty segment. Some or all of the mucilage is left on the bean during drying, creating a middle ground between washed and natural processing. Produces balanced sweetness, medium body, and stone fruit complexity.

Best for: Mid-range specialty buyers, café operators seeking crowd-pleasing single-origin options, and subscription coffee roasters.

Natural / Dry Process

Less common in Temanggung due to the region's humidity, but available in limited quantities. Cherries are dried whole, imparting intensely fruity, wine-like, full-bodied character to the cup.

Best for: Adventurous specialty markets, single-origin espresso buyers, premium retail with high-demand consumers, and competition lot programs.

5. Export Grade Classifications

Indonesia's coffee export grading follows the SNI (Standar Nasional Indonesia) system, aligned with international standards. For roasted bean exports, the SCA (Specialty Coffee Association) scoring protocol applies to specialty-grade lots.

SNI Grade Classification (Green Bean Basis)

GradeMax Defects per 300gSCA ScoreTypical Market
Specialty (SCA)≤ 5 primary defects≥ 80 pointsPremium single-origin, specialty retail, direct trade
Grade 1≤ 11 defects80–84Specialty and premium commercial
Grade 2≤ 25 defects75–79Premium commercial blends
Grade 3≤ 44 defects—Standard commercial blends
Grade 4a≤ 60 defects—Industrial and instant coffee
Grade 4b≤ 80 defects—Industrial processing

Reputable Temanggung exporters work exclusively with Grade 1 and Specialty-grade green beans before roasting to ensure consistent cup quality across commercial shipments. For buyers sourcing from new suppliers, always request a green bean grading report and cupping score from a certified Q Grader before committing to a commercial order.

6. Minimum Order Quantities (MOQ)

MOQ for roasted coffee exports from Temanggung varies by buyer type, processing complexity, and packaging format. The following tiers reflect standard market practice.

MOQ by Buyer Type

Buyer TypeMOQNotes
Sample Order0.5–2 kg per SKUFor cupping evaluation; not for resale
Boutique Importer / Specialty Café30–60 kgTypically air freight
Small Distributor100–300 kgMixed varieties or roast levels allowed
Mid-size Importer / Roaster500 kg – 1 MTSea freight recommended
Large Commercial Buyer5 MT and aboveFCL (Full Container Load) possible
Private Label / Contract Roasting200 kg minimum per SKURequires agreed roast profile and packaging spec

Mixed-SKU orders: Most Temanggung exporters allow mixed-variety or mixed-roast-level orders as long as the combined weight meets the minimum threshold. A buyer can order 50 kg of light-roast Arabica and 50 kg of medium-roast Robusta to meet a 100 kg MOQ.

Specialty micro-lots: Due to limited harvest volumes, traceable single-farm lots typically carry a per-SKU minimum of 20–30 kg. Buyers interested in these lots should plan sourcing 6–12 months ahead of desired delivery, aligned to the harvest calendar.

Price Components Explained

Understanding what contributes to the FOB price helps buyers plan landed costs and negotiate more effectively:

Buyers requiring custom branding, proprietary roast profiles, or specialized flavor development should budget an additional $1.00–$3.00/kg above standard pricing. A non-recurring setup fee of $200–$800 may apply for private label packaging design approval and roast profile calibration.

8. Packaging Options for Export

Correct packaging is critical for preserving roasted coffee freshness during international transit — which can range from 3 days (air to Singapore) to 35 days (sea freight to Europe).

Standard Export Packaging Formats

FormatDescriptionShelf Life (Sealed)Best For
1 kg one-way valve bag (kraft)Food-grade kraft paper with internal foil/plastic lining and CO₂ degassing valve; optional resealable zipper.6–12 monthsSpecialty retail, e-commerce, and high-volume café operations.
250g / 500g valve bagRetail-ready boutique packaging; customizable with optional clear windows and tear-notches.6–12 monthsDirect-to-consumer (D2C), specialty grocery, and boutique retail.
5 kg bulk bag (foil)High-barrier multi-layer foil with commercial one-way valve; typically nitrogen-flushed to preserve freshness.12–18 monthsHoreca (Hotels, Restaurants, Cafés), institutional food service, and small-batch roasters.
Custom OEM / Private LabelBuyer-specified dimensions, materials (e.g., recyclable or compostable), custom printing, and branding.Per specificationEstablished private label programs and international brand expansions.

Degassing requirement: All roasted coffee for export must be allowed to degas for 24–72 hours after roasting before sealing, to prevent bag bloating and ensure valve integrity during shipping. Confirm this practice with your supplier.

Nitrogen-flushed packaging is strongly recommended for sea freight shipments exceeding 20 days transit time. This extends shelf life to 12–18 months and ensures product arrives in optimal condition.

Not all Temanggung exporters hold all certifications. Buyers with specific requirements should communicate this at the earliest stage of supplier conversations — certified lots often carry a price premium and may have limited annual availability.

Import-Side Compliance (Buyer's Responsibility by Market)


MarketKey Regulatory & Import Requirements
European Union

General Food Law: Compliance with Regulation (EC) 178/2002 trace-hygiene frameworks.


Contaminants & Pesticides: Strict enforcement of maximum residue limits (MRLs) per Regulation (EC) 396/2005.


EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR): Following official amendments, large/medium operators must fully comply by December 30, 2026 (micro/small enterprises by June 30, 2027). Soluble coffee is officially included in the compliance scope. Requires mandatory plot-level geolocation data (polygons for plots over 4 hectares) to verify zero deforestation linkages post-December 31, 2020.

United States

FDA Prior Notice: Must be filed electronically and approved prior to the shipment arriving at the port of entry.


FSMA / FSVP: Importers must comply with the Foreign Supplier Verification Program, establishing robust quality assurance and hazard-control verification for Indonesian mills.


Registration: Processing facilities must maintain valid Bioterrorism Act registration.

Japan

Food Sanitation Act: Administered by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW).


Positive List System: Strict enforcement of agricultural chemical residue thresholds. Japanese customs executes stringent random lot testing for imported coffee, holding shipments at the port if unlisted chemical traces are discovered.

Australia / New Zealand

Biosecurity Import Conditions (BICON): Regulated by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF). Requires precise moisture management and insect-free packaging to pass border quarantine inspections.


Labeling: Mandatory compliance with Country of Origin Labelling (CoOL) requirements for all retail-packaged roasted coffee.

GCC / Middle East

Halal Attestation: Official Halal certification is strongly preferred and increasingly requested by retail distributors across the Gulf region.


Documentation: Demands notarized Certificates of Origin, commercial invoices, and legalized shipping manifests certified by the destination embassy or consulate.

Critical note for EU buyers: The EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) is a compliance priority for all Temanggung coffee sourced into Europe. Buyers must work with suppliers who have begun EUDR compliance mapping — including geolocation documentation at farm or plot level. A growing number of Temanggung cooperatives and exporters are actively preparing this documentation.

Primary Port of Choice: Represents the most cost-effective and shortest inland trucking haul (typically 2–3 hours via overland roads). This route minimizes local transit hazards and lowers the carbon footprint of the domestic supply chain. It is highly optimized for Less-than-Container Load (LCL) consolidation of specialty coffee lots or Full Container Load (FCL) regional feeder loops.
Tanjung Priok (IDTPP)

Jakarta, DKI Jakarta


(~430 km from Temanggung)

Strategic Alternative: Though it requires a significantly longer overland haul across the Trans-Java Toll Road, Jakarta provides a vastly superior network of direct global main-line ocean carriers. This eliminates regional transshipment delays (e.g., bypassing Singapore hubs) and offers more flexible container spot-rate options, making it ideal for large-volume industrial or commercial contracts bound for North American and European ports.

11. Step-by-Step Sourcing Process

Step 1 — Define Your Requirements

Before contacting any supplier, prepare a clear specification sheet covering: desired variety (Arabica / Robusta / blend), processing method, roast level, grade, packaging format, MOQ, certifications required, and target destination port.

Step 2 — Identify and Vet Qualified Exporters

Reliable sourcing channels include:

- AEKI (Asosiasi Eksportir Kopi Indonesia) — directory of registered Indonesian coffee exporters

- SCAI (Specialty Coffee Association of Indonesia) — specialty-focused producers and exporters

- Algrano (algrano.com) — direct trade platform connecting international roasters with Indonesian exporters

- Indonesia International Coffee Festival (IICF) and CA Expo — direct access to Temanggung producers

Due diligence checklist before finalizing a supplier:

- [ ] Valid Indonesian Export License (API-U or API-P)

- [ ] Phytosanitary Certificate issuance capability

- [ ] SCA Q Grader on staff or access to a certified cupping lab

- [ ] BPOM food safety certification for roasted/processed product

- [ ] References from at least two existing international clients

- [ ] Ability to send 200–500g cupping samples via international courier

- [ ] Transparent farm or cooperative traceability documentation

- [ ] Clear payment terms and dispute resolution policy

Step 3 — Request and Cup Samples

Always request samples before placing a commercial order. Sample fees typically range from $15–$50 (often waived on first commercial order). DHL/FedEx express shipping costs are typically borne by the buyer. Cup samples against your target profile and communicate feedback using SCA flavor wheel terminology to allow the exporter to dial in the roast specification.

Step 4 — Negotiate Terms and Place Order

Agree on: price per kg (FOB or CIF), MOQ, payment terms, delivery timeline, packaging specs, quality specification, and rejection protocol.

Standard payment terms:

- First-time buyers: 100% upfront T/T (telegraphic transfer) or irrevocable Letter of Credit (L/C)

- Established buyers: 30% deposit + 70% balance before shipment, or 30/70 against Bill of Lading copy

Step 5 — Monitor Production and Shipment

For premium orders, request roast logs, sensory evaluation reports (cupping scores, moisture readings, Agtron measurements), and pre-shipment moisture data as part of the shipment documentation package. Work with a freight forwarder familiar with agricultural commodity imports to ensure all customs documents are in order before cargo arrival.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Temanggung coffee available as roasted (not just green) for export?

Yes. Unlike many Indonesian origins where only green beans are exported, Temanggung has a growing community of specialty roasters with the capability to roast, package, and export finished roasted coffee directly to international buyers. This is particularly convenient for smaller importers, subscription coffee businesses, and specialty retailers who do not operate their own roasting facilities.

What makes Temanggung coffee different from Sumatra Mandheling?

Both are Indonesian coffees with full body and low acidity, but Temanggung tends to be cleaner, less musty, and more nuanced. Its distinctive tobacco and dark chocolate character — a product of unique intercropping terroir — gives it a complexity that diverges meaningfully from the heavier, more rustic earthiness of Sumatran profiles. Temanggung Arabica is also notably brighter and more fruit-forward than most Sumatran Arabicas.

What SCA score should I expect from specialty-grade Temanggung lots?

Well-processed specialty lots from Temanggung consistently score 83–87 SCA points from certified Q Graders. Top micro-lots and competition-grade offerings occasionally reach 88+. Always request the cupping score from a certified Q Grader — not a self-assessed score — before purchasing specialty-designated product.

What is the lead time from order confirmation to FOB shipment?

For standard in-stock roasted products: 7–14 days (including post-roast degassing). For custom roast profiles or micro-lot sourcing during harvest season: 3–8 weeks. Plan logistics timelines accordingly, particularly for first orders.

Is Temanggung coffee EUDR compliant for EU import?

EUDR compliance is the buyer's responsibility under EU regulation, but requires cooperation from suppliers. Ask your Temanggung supplier specifically whether they have begun farm geolocation mapping and traceability documentation for EUDR compliance. A growing number of Temanggung cooperatives are actively preparing this documentation for EU-bound export.

Are organic-certified lots available from Temanggung?

Yes, in limited quantities. A number of Temanggung smallholder cooperatives hold USDA or EU Organic certification. Organic lots carry a premium of $0.50–$2.00/kg and must be sourced in advance due to limited annual supply. Communicate organic requirements at the earliest stage of supplier conversations.

What is the typical payment structure for new buyer relationships?

First-time buyers are generally required to pay 100% upfront by T/T or open an irrevocable Letter of Credit. Established relationships typically move to 30% deposit + 70% balance before shipment or against Bill of Lading copy. Some exporters on platforms like Algrano offer payment protection through the platform for additional security.

Conclusion

Temanggung is one of Indonesia's most commercially compelling and underutilized coffee origins. Its ability to produce both export-grade Fine Robusta and specialty-quality Arabica from a single Highland regency in Central Java makes it genuinely versatile for buyers serving multiple market segments simultaneously. The tobacco-spice terroir character is authentic, distinctive, and increasingly recognized by international specialty buyers as a differentiated origin narrative.

For commercial buyers, the combination of competitive FOB pricing, Grade 1 and specialty-grade product availability, growing roaster infrastructure for export-ready roasted product, and the potential of Fine Robusta for espresso markets makes Temanggung a strategically attractive sourcing destination in 2025 and beyond.

Successful sourcing requires diligence: verify supplier credentials, specify processing methods clearly, plan around the harvest calendar for fresh lots, comply with destination market import requirements (particularly EUDR for EU buyers), and invest in genuine long-term relationships with the farmers and cooperatives that produce this exceptional coffee.

The cup quality you will discover in Temanggung may well surprise you — and your customers.
